poc_plan: Week 0: Baseline collection — 500 seed prompts from support + 1000 doc pairs for search parity tests.
Week 1: Hosted API POC — run OpenAI-compat endpoint with Redwood Hosted, measure latency, token cost, and answer quality.
Week 2: Regression sweep — automated evals against held-out prompt set; check hallucination and F1/recall for search.
Acceptance criteria: p95 response latency <= 250ms for short-chat flows, embeddings recall >= 0.82 vs baseline, <5% increase in hallucination rate, cost reduction >= 15% on tokens or equivalent.
If POC passes: schedule Dedicated sizing workshop and commit negotiation (target May 2026).
technical_requirements: Latency SLO: p95 <= 250ms for chat (short-turn), p99 < 600ms for critical UI calls.
Throughput: sustained 200 reqs/sec for embeddings pipeline (nightly bulk + realtime spikes).
Model preferences: open to Falcon/Mistral variants but must match/infer parity with current OpenAI outputs; prefer a deterministic version for canary traffic.
Routing/fallback: want automatic fallback to cheaper quantized model for non-critical routes and canary split by route.
Prefix/KV caching important for chat context reuse to keep cost down.
migration_concerns: Prompt parity: tokenization differences + system message handling produced subtle differences in answers during initial tests.
Function call compatibility: map current function-call payloads exactly; first demo showed name mismatch on some tool calls.
Streaming semantics: client expects chunked deltas; need to confirm identical framing to avoid SDK changes.
Regression monitoring: team wants Red-flag alerts if hallucination increases or regression in rank for search queries.
Data residency + logs: must ensure Hosted keeps PII out of logs or route to Dedicated/VPC for regulated customers.
